retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note (or its Fact rows), always RETURN its citation metadata
alongside the text — document/file name, title or note_type, and page_no/printed_page (or
page_start/page_end) — not just the text field alone. The judgment step that reads your
transcript afterward has to cite an exact document/section/page for every passage it relies
on and can only do that with what you hand it here.

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over
writing the equivalent raw Cypher yourself in query_puppygraph — it runs a traversal that's
already known to be correct, rather than one you reconstruct from the schema notes each time.

Patient name, MRN, date of birth, and (for some review types) claim_number itself — even when
they appear inline inside a Note's or Fact's text, not just as their own property — are
de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] or [[CLAIM-0005]], not real values. The double
brackets are literal characters of the value, not markdown or wiki-link markup to strip out —
verified live: passing a "cleaned up" claim_number with the brackets removed as a tool argument
silently matches zero rows (the underlying property is the bracketed token, not the bare text
inside it), which then looks like the record has no data at all. Copy a token byte-for-byte,
brackets included, everywhere it's used: as a tool call argument, in Cypher, and quoted verbatim
in a citation. Never remark on the token format, guess what real value it stands for, or treat
its presence as unusual — a separate step restores the real values afterward, outside anything
you do here.

Once you've gathered the claim line detail, the governing policy, and at least one relevant
medical-record passage, stop calling tools and reply with a short plain-text note of what you
found. Do NOT render a Finding/No Finding determination yourself — a separate step decides
that from what you retrieve here. Don't fabricate or guess at data you haven't queried.

4. Query the medical record notes for relevant documentation to support the selected diagnoses and procedures.

You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Teach-back is documented\nfor each session. Learning barriers: critical illness and delirium early in the course; participation improved with recovery. Interpreter not\nrequired (English).\nNorepinephrine (Levophed)\nPurpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.\nDose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.\nSide Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.\nMonitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.\nVancomycin\nPurpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.\nDose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.\nSide Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).\nMonitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.\nTeach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.\nPiperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)\nPurpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.\nDose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.\nSide Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).\nMonitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.\nTeach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.\nPantoprazole (Protonix)\nPurpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.\nDose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.\nSide Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.\nMonitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.\nTeach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.\nEnoxaparin (Lovenox)\nPurpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.\nDose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.\nSide Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).\nMonitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.\nTeach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call\nfor help (unusual bleeding).\nInsulin infusion / Sliding scale\nPurpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.\nDose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.\nSide Effects\nLow blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.\nMonitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.\nTeach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.\nAmiodarone\nPurpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).\nDose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.\nSide Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use\nsunscreen.\nMonitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials\nprovided.\nApixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge\nPurpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).\nDose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.\nSide Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.\nMonitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.\nTeach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid\nibuprofen. result.system_note: What was billed: Principal Dx billed as K85.90 (acute pancreatitis, unspecified) with additional pancreatitis codes K85.11 (biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) and K85.82 (acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis), sepsis/septic shock codes (R65.21, A41.50, B96.1), respiratory failure/ARDS codes (J96.01, J80), and procedures including endotracheal intubation and >96-hour ventilation (0BH17EZ; 5A1D90Z). What the record actually documents (key citations): - Infected pancreatic necrosis with identified organism (Klebsiella pneumoniae) and biliary/gallstone etiology: History & Physical (Admitting) active problem list contains "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae" and "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology." (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946). These items establish infected, gallstone-related necrotizing pancreatitis rather than an uninfected necrosis or non-specific pancreatitis. (See evidence excerpts below.) - Microbiology/treatment and source control consistent with infected necrosis: Discharge/Transfer Summary documents "infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16," confirming an organism-identified infection that was managed (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086). - Septic shock physiology on admission and vasopressor support: Admission labs and orders show elevated lactate ("lactate 4.6 mmol/L") and nursing/provider orders include vasopressor support ("norepinephrine to MAP >= 65") (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946). The Hospital Problem List lists "Septic shock | R65.21 | 05/29/2026 | Resolved | Off vasopressors day 10," indicating septic shock onset on admission (Hospital Problem List, Hospital Problem List, p. 9-9). - Respiratory failure and mechanical ventilation: multiple ICU progress notes and a Procedure Note document intubation for respiratory failure (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p. 44-44: "Indication for Procedure: Respiratory failure from pancreatitis and pain") and the Discharge Summary documents extubation on ICU day 18 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086), establishing ventilatory support >96 hours and supporting J96.01 and the ventilator-duration procedure code. Why this fails as billed (policy + documentation linkage): 1) Conflicting pancreatitis codes / principal diagnosis specificity: the chart documents necrotizing, infected, gallstone pancreatitis with organism identified. Coding both K85.11 (biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) and K85.82 (acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) on the same stay is internally inconsistent (one states uninfected necrosis, the other infected necrosis). Further, the principal diagnosis billed as K85.90 (unspecified) is less specific than the record supports. The record supports a specific infected necrotizing biliary pancreatitis as the principal diagnosis (see Admission H&P and Discharge Summary) - therefore principal should be the infected necrosis code (K85.82) rather than K85.90 or the uninfected code K85.11 (contradicted by the clinical documentation cited). 2) Sepsis organism specificity and sepsis/septic-shock coding: the microbiology and provider documentation identify Klebsiella pneumoniae as the infecting organism and the team treated with meropenem (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086; History & Physical active problem list). The R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) documentation requirements in policy require provider documentation of septic shock plus objective evidence (vasopressor use, lactate elevation) - all present in the chart (Policy: Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx; see criterion for vasopressor + lactate). Given the organism is identified, the appropriate organism-specific A41 code is A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) rather than A41.50 (gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) combined with B96.1. The policy ICD-10 selection guide explicitly lists Klebsiella pneumoniae -> A41.53 (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria table). Using A41.50 + B96.1 is therefore a mis-specification (higher-risk for miscoding) when organism-specific sepsis code exists and the provider documents the organism. 3) POA flags appear incorrect for several conditions: the clinical timeline shows septic shock, respiratory failure/ARDS, and infected necrosis present at or shortly after presentation (ED/H&P note documents multi-organ dysfunction, high lactate, intubation, and vasopressor use on admission). However the claim has POA=N for key codes (K85.82, A41.50, J80). The Hospital Problem List, ED note, and Admission H&P all document these conditions at presentation (supporting POA=Y); POA indicators on the claim should be corrected to match the chart (e.g., R65.21 POA=Y per problem list/admission). The R65.21 policy also notes POA must reflect whether shock was present on admission vs developed later (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Medical - Septic Shock Confirmed on Admission Pathway). 4) Respiratory failure / ventilation coding is supported: objective oxygenation data (ABG/SpO2/PF ratios in the notes), procedure note of intubation, and documented ventilation duration/extubation day support J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) and the ventilator-duration procedure code (policy presumption that invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure satisfies objective criteria is met) (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx; see Presumption rule regarding mechanical ventilation). Action to correct coding (complete corrected sets): - Revised principal diagnosis (position 1): K85.82 - Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis (infected necrosis explicitly documented and organism identified). Remove the uninfected necrosis code K85.11 and the unspecified K85.90 (both contradicted or redundant given documented infected necrosis). - Replace sepsis code A41.50 + organism code B96.1 with the organism-specific sepsis code A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) and retain R65.21 (severe sepsis/septic shock) as an additional MCC-level code because septic shock (vasopressor + lactate) is documented. - Correct POA flags to reflect these conditions were present on admission (per Admission H&P, ED note, and Hospital Problem List). Specifically: K85.82 POA=Y; R65.21 POA=Y; A41.53 POA=Y; J80 POA=Y (ARDS documented at/near admission). - Keep the remaining supported comorbidities (diverticulitis with perforation/abscess, gallstone disease, AKI, AF, new-onset diabetes, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, GERD) as coded where supported by chart/problem list. - Procedures as billed (endotracheal intubation, feeding device placement, percutaneous drainage(s), VARD-related PCS entries, PICC insertion/monitoring device, and ventilator >96 hours) are supported by procedure notes, progress notes, and the discharge summary; leave procedure list unchanged but recommend coding validation to align exact PCS root operations/approach with operative/procedure notes (e.g., VARD vs. "excision" language). Key citations (audit trail): - History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946 - "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology."; and Active Problem List entry "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae." - Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086 - "infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16," and "Extubation was successful on ICU day 18 following resolution of ARDS." - History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 861-946 - laboratory data: "lactate 4.6 mmol/L." and orders: "Hemodynamics: aggressive volume resuscitation with balanced crystalloid; norepinephrine to MAP >= 65; monitor for abdominal compartment syndrome." - Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p. 44-44 - "Indication for Procedure: Respiratory failure from pancreatitis and pain" (supports endotracheal intubation and attribution to respiratory failure). - Hospital Problem List, Hospital Problem List, p. 9-9 - "Septic shock | R65.21 | 05/29/2026 | Resolved | Off vasopressors day 10." - Policy guidance: Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx (R65.21 validation criteria: vasopressor + lactate and organism identification pathways) and Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx (J96.01 presumption rule when invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure). Conclusion: The clinical record supports infected, gallstone-related necrotizing pancreatitis with Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis and septic shock, respiratory failure requiring prolonged ventilation, and AKI. However, the submitted claim miscoded the pancreatitis specificity and sepsis organism specificity and has incorrect POA indicators on multiple high-severity codes. Therefore this claim is a Finding. The complete corrected diagnosis and procedure sets are provided below for reconciliation and resubmission. Documents cited above are available in the chart and are enumerated explicitly in evidence_cited for line-by-line audit verification.
result.rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit determination - MR_14 (Admission 05/29/2026) To: Coding/Medical Records Department, We completed a clinical audit of the inpatient record for MR_14. The audit found that several high-severity diagnosis codes on the claim are miscoded or mis-specified relative to the treating-provider documentation and governing coding policy. Specifically, the chart documents infected necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with an identified organism (Klebsiella pneumoniae), septic shock requiring vasopressors and with elevated lactate, and respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation over 96 consecutive hours. These clinical facts require more specific diagnosis coding than was billed. Finding (summary): - The principal diagnosis and pancreatitis coding are incorrect as submitted. The medical record documents infected pancreatic necrosis (Klebsiella pneumoniae) related to gallstones. The claim lists K85.90 (unspecified) as principal and also K85.11 (biliary pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) plus K85.82 (infected necrosis). The combined/bundled use of an "uninfected necrosis" code alongside documentation of infected necrosis is inconsistent with the clinical record and ICD-10-CM coding principles. The chart supports K85.82 (acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) as the principal diagnosis. - Sepsis coding: the organism is identified (Klebsiella pneumoniae) and treated; therefore the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code is A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae). The claim's use of A41.50 (gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) plus B96.1 (Klebsiella as cause) is a mis-specification per the sepsis code selection guidance when an organism-specific A41 code is available. - POA indicators on the submitted claim do not match the chart. Documentation indicates septic shock, respiratory failure/ARDS, and infected necrosis were present at or very near admission; these should be flagged POA=Y where appropriate. Basis (clinical + policy excerpts relied upon): - Infected necrosis and identified organism: History & Physical (Admitting) active problem list includes "Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae" and imaging documents 40-50% pancreatic necrosis; Discharge summary documents source control (CT-guided drainage and VARD) and meropenem therapy for Klebsiella (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 861-946; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086). - Septic shock physiology on admission: lactate >2 and vasopressor orders documented (norepinephrine to MAP >= 65) and Hospital Problem List lists R65.21 with onset 05/29/2026 (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 861-946; Hospital Problem List, p. 9-9). Policy for R65.21 requires documentation of septic shock (vasopressor + lactate criteria) and an organism pathway when organism identified (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx). - Respiratory failure and >96-hour ventilation: procedure note documents intubation for respiratory failure and Discharge Summary documents extubation on ICU day 18 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1085-1086; Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p. 44-44). The J96.01 policy permits presumption of the objective hypoxemia criterion when invasive mechanical ventilation is documented and attributed to respiratory failure (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx). Correction required (what we changed): - Principal diagnosis (position 1): change to K85.82 - Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis. Remove K85.90 (unspecified) and K85.11 (biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) as inconsistent with documentation of infected necrosis. - Replace A41.50 + B96.1 with A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) and retain R65.21 for severe sepsis with septic shock (MCC), as vasopressors and elevated lactate are documented. - Correct POA flags to reflect that infected necrosis, septic shock, respiratory failure/ARDS were present on admission (POA=Y) per Admission H&P/ED notes and Hospital Problem List. - Retain and validate procedure codes related to intubation, >96-hour ventilator support, percutaneous drainage, VARD, feeding device insertion, and vascular/PICC monitoring device placement - these are supported by procedure notes and the discharge summary; coder validation should ensure PCS root operations/approach match operative/procedure detail. Corrected diagnosis set (complete, position 1 = principal): 1. K85.82 2. K57.21 3. K80.2 4. R65.21 5. A41.53 6. J96.01 7. J80 8. N17.9 9. I48.91 10. E11.6 11. K86.8 12. I10 13. E78.5 14. K21.9 Corrected procedure set (complete): - 0BH17EZ - Insertion of endotracheal airway into trachea, via natural or artificial opening - 0DH64UZ - Insertion of feeding device into stomach, percutaneous endoscopic approach - 0FBG3ZZ - Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach (VARD/excision coding should be validated against operative note) - 0F9G30Z - Drainage of pancreas with drainage device, percutaneous approach - 0W9G3ZZ - Drainage of peritoneal cavity, percutaneous approach - 02HV33Z - Insertion of infusion device into superior vena cava, percutaneous approach (PICC/infusion device) - 03HY32Z - Insertion of monitoring device into upper artery, percutaneous approach (arterial line) - 5A1D90Z - Assistance with respiratory ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours Disposition documented: transfer to Long-Term Acute Care Hospital (Transfer Instructions / Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1082-1086). If you disagree with these corrections, please provide specific physician attestation or CDI documentation supporting the retained alternative codes (e.g., explicit provider documentation that necrosis was uninfected, or that Klebsiella was NOT the etiology of sepsis), and we will reconsider. Otherwise, please implement the corrected code set and POA indicators on the claim. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team
